_comment: Ordered provider lanes, and within each an ordered model fallback list.
Model names live here and NEVER in code: free catalogues churn, and providers have been
observed silently deleting free models. A 404 falls through to the next entry and logs loudly.
rpm sits deliberately under the published ceiling - those numbers are not guaranteed and are
no longer documented per model.
LANE ORDER IS THE COST POLICY. The router walks this list top to bottom, so the free lanes are
tried first and the paid ones only answer what the free tiers could not. Move a paid lane up
if you would rather have its quality on every line and are willing to pay for it.
A lane with no key entered is skipped in silence, so shipping openai and anthropic enabled
costs nothing until someone deliberately pastes a key into Settings.
2026-08: the entire Gemini 2.x list died and this is what that churn actually looks like.
gemini-2.0-flash was shut down on 1 June 2026 - a guaranteed 404 that had been sitting in this
file as the middle fallback. gemini-2.5-flash and -flash-lite both began returning 404 'no
longer available' to NEWLY CREATED keys around 9 July, while Google's own deprecation page
still lists them as active with no shutdown date. So the same file worked on an older key and
failed completely on a new one, which is exactly how it was found. Their real shutdown is
16 October 2026.
gemini-2.5-flash stays LAST because keys created before July can still use it, and it costs
nothing to try after the others. gemini-2.5-flash-lite is dropped rather than kept beside it:
one tail entry for a dying family is a fallback, two is noise in the log.
2026-08, and within hours of the Gemini fix: Groq's list had died too, which is how the app
came to show 'translation failed' with two keys that both passed the key test. Groq deprecated
qwen/qwen3-32b and llama-3.3-70b-versatile on 17 June 2026 and stopped serving them during
August. Both free lanes were therefore empty at the same time, and the app's only symptom was
the English fallback - the router did exactly what it promises and there was simply nothing
left to route to. Replaced with the two production models Groq itself names as the migration
target. qwen/qwen3.6-27b is deliberately NOT included: it is preview-tier, and preview is what
churns. Their Arabic has not been compared against the old llama model - nobody has measured
it, so if the Arabic reads worse after this change, that is the reason and it is worth saying
out loud rather than assuming the lane is simply 'working' again.
The lesson from having this happen twice in one day: a lane whose every model is gone is not a
rare event, it is the normal end of a free model's life, and it arrives without warning. Check
both lanes against each provider's own /models endpoint before blaming anything else.
Order within the lane is preference, and it is deliberately NOT newest-first. 3.5-flash and
3.1-flash-lite are the two Google was listing on the free tier in July 2026; 3.6-flash is newer
but its free-tier status is unconfirmed, and a paid-only model at the top of this list costs
every free user a failed round trip on every single line before the fallthrough saves them.
Free-and-confirmed beats new-and-maybe. Google no longer publishes per-model free limits at
all - they are only visible in AI Studio for your own project - so this cannot be checked from
documentation and is reasoned from what the pricing page showed.
The two paid lanes' model names were checked against each provider's own model list in
August 2026. 'gpt-5.6' is deliberately the alias rather than 'gpt-5.6-sol' it points at, so a
point release does not strand this file; terra and luna are the cheaper variants behind it.
If one is ever retired the router says so by name in the Diagnostics log and falls through.
